experiment_note: Run 3 of codex_think_ec: same as the v5 label (thinking, end condition, 500-iteration cap, context summarization with a fit guarantee, kernel-enforced write gate, evaluator-side final submission, 7200 s agent budget, no spend cap, retrying shim), plus: every tool call runs under a supervisor with a wall-clock deadline that kills the whole process tree including background/detached children (60 s default, 300 s max, an invalid timeout is rejected outright, not silently defaulted); a run where cleanup cannot be confirmed is an infrastructure error, not graded; DeepSeek's native tool-call syntax (DSML) is recovered into a real tool call instead of being discarded when it leaks as plain text; the submission client has its own bounded budget (200 s) nested inside a 240 s tool deadline and classifies a rate-limited (HTTP 429) reply distinctly from 'no result'. Earlier runs of this experiment: codex_think_ec (v4, stopped, kept as evidence) and codex_think_ec_v5 (stopped: tool-call leak losing rounds + unbounded background loops hammering the submission server; 5 passed, 1 failed, 19 operator-stopped; see D39).
